general: The Dead Sea's surface is over 430 meters below sea level, the lowest point on Earth's land surface.
Vatican City is the smallest country in the world by both area and population.
Russia spans 11 time zones, more than any other country.
The Six-Day War in 1967 lasted exactly six days and reshaped the map of the Middle East.
Jerusalem has been besieged, attacked, captured and recaptured dozens of times throughout recorded history.
The word 'Torah' literally means 'teaching' or 'instruction' in Hebrew, not simply 'law'.
The Dead Sea Scrolls, found in caves near Qumran, include the oldest known copies of Hebrew Bible texts.
Mount Olympus in Greek mythology was believed to be the literal home of the twelve major gods.
The Norse concept of Ragnarok describes a prophesied end-of-world battle, after which the world is reborn.
The Sefirot in Kabbalah are ten attributes through which the Infinite is said to reveal itself in creation.
The Suez Canal, central to the 1956 Suez Crisis, connects the Mediterranean Sea directly to the Red Sea.
Nepal is the only country in the world whose national flag is not rectangular.
The Talmud is not a single book but a vast compiled record of centuries of rabbinic debate.
The 1973 Yom Kippur War began on Judaism's holiest day, catching Israel by surprise.
Ancient Egyptian mythology held that the heart, not the brain, was the seat of intelligence and emotion.
Iceland has no standing army, navy, or air force — one of very few countries without one.
The Zohar, Kabbalah's central text, is written mostly in Aramaic, not Hebrew.
Bhutan measures national progress using 'Gross National Happiness' instead of GDP.
The 1948 Arab-Israeli War is referred to by Israelis as the War of Independence and by Palestinians as the Nakba.
The Great Wall of China is not visible to the naked eye from space, despite the popular myth.
Israel is one of only a handful of countries in the world that entered the 21st century with more forest cover than it had a century earlier, due to large-scale afforestation.
The Hebrew calendar is lunisolar, meaning it adds a leap month roughly every three years to stay aligned with the solar year.
The 1979 Egypt-Israel peace treaty was the first peace agreement between Israel and an Arab nation.
The world's smallest recognized country by population is Vatican City, with under 1,000 residents.
The Talmud describes two major components: the Mishnah (compiled law) and the Gemara (commentary and debate on the Mishnah).
Zeus, king of the Greek gods, was said to have overthrown his own father, Cronus, to take power.
The Kabbalistic concept of 'tikkun olam' — repairing the world — has become a widely used phrase in modern Jewish social action.
Masada, an ancient fortress in Israel, is famous for a mass siege during the First Jewish-Roman War around 73 CE.
France is the most visited country in the world by international tourist arrivals.
The Dome of the Rock in Jerusalem, completed in 691 CE, is one of the oldest surviving works of Islamic architecture.
In Norse mythology, Yggdrasil is a giant ash tree said to connect all nine worlds.
The 1993 Oslo Accords were the first direct agreement between Israel and the Palestine Liberation Organization.
Timbuktu, in modern Mali, was once a major center of Islamic scholarship and manuscript production.
The word 'Israel' itself is generally understood to mean 'one who struggles with God,' from the biblical account of Jacob.
Machu Picchu was unknown to the wider world until it was brought to international attention in 1911.
The Egyptian god Anubis, associated with mummification, is often depicted with the head of a jackal.
Antarctica is the only continent with no native human population and no official time zone of its own.
The Balfour Declaration of 1917 was a public statement by the British government expressing support for a Jewish homeland in Palestine.
